# Architecture

## Quarto manages the system; focused tools do the rendering

```{=latex}
\centering
\resizebox{0.93\textwidth}{!}{\input{figures/how-pieces-fit.tex}}
```

## The package bundle is a toolbox, not one giant preamble

- Quarto: profiles, citations, code blocks, cross-references, reproducible builds
- LuaLaTeX: Unicode text and mathematics
- `siunitx` + `mhchem`: engineering quantities and chemistry
- TikZ + domain extensions: process meaning and diagrams
- PGFPlots: retained values with document-matched typography

::: {.alert}
Load a tool when the page visibly needs its job.
:::

# Chemical-engineering notation

## Equations, units, and reactions share one notation system

$$
V\frac{\partial C_A}{\partial t}
=F(C_{A,0}-C_A)-VkC_A
$$

```{=latex}
\begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
\column{0.48\textwidth}
\begin{block}{Operating point}
$T=\SI{355.2}{\kelvin}$\\
$P=\SI{4.7}{\barunit}$\\
$\dot n=\SI{12.2}{\kmol\per\hour}$
\end{block}
\column{0.48\textwidth}
\begin{block}{Reaction}
\centering
\ce{CO2 + 2 RNH2 <=> RNHCOO- + RNH3+}
\end{block}
\end{columns}
```

# Quantitative evidence

## PGFPlots keeps models, observations, and uncertainty distinct

```{=latex}
\centering
\resizebox{0.94\textwidth}{!}{\input{figures/quantitative-plots.tex}}
```

## Coordinate systems should match the physical question

```{=latex}
\centering
\resizebox{0.90\textwidth}{!}{\input{figures/composition-and-polar.tex}}
```

- Ternary axes: composition data normalized to a declared mass or mole basis.
- Polar axes: cyclic or directional responses with physical angular meaning.
- Patch plots: small reviewed meshes only; data-rich fields belong in analysis code.

## A patch plot is useful only while the mesh stays reviewable

```{=latex}
\centering
\resizebox{0.78\textwidth}{!}{\input{figures/patch-field.tex}}
```

The values are illustrative; a real field must retain mesh connectivity,
units, and provenance with the plotted table.

# Reusable authoring

## Quarto profiles keep article and Beamer ownership separate

```yaml
# article.qmd
format:
  pdf:
    pdf-engine: lualatex
    include-in-header: tex/article-preamble.tex

# deck.qmd
format:
  beamer:
    pdf-engine: lualatex
    theme: moloch
    include-in-header: tex/beamer-preamble.tex
```

## The working rule is simple

1. Keep calculations and fitted values in analysis code.
2. Retain the exact tables used for claims.
3. Let TikZ or PGFPlots render the smallest useful visual.
4. Let Quarto produce the article and presentation profiles.
5. Inspect both PDFs before release.

::: {.alert}
The bundle is successful when every loaded tool has a visible job and every
number has a traceable basis.
:::

## Compilation is not a visual acceptance test

- Reserve label zones away from pipes, arrows, and page edges.
- Use one semantic demonstration per panel and one coordinate system per panel.
- Add source-level clearance below the lowest diagram node.
- Design shared figures at the smaller article or Beamer placement.
- Inspect every rendered page at full size; use contact sheets only for flow.

`chktex`, `lacheck`, and `texfot` help with source and log defects. Raster
inspection owns overlap, clipping, and legibility.

## Backup: narrow tools remain available

`standalone`, `subfiles`, `import`, `xr-hyper`, `pdfpages`, `pdflscape`,
`longtable`, `csvsimple`, `tcolorbox`, `algorithmicx`, `listings`, `latexdiff`,
`lineno`, `todonotes`, `appendixnumberbeamer`, `pdfpc`, `animate`, and `svg`
remain conditional tools. Add them only for the feature their nameable job
requires.
